newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks end with slight gain in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks end with slight gain in light trade.

text.p: Chilean stocks closed narrowly higher on Tuesday after a sluggish session highlighted by a sharp decline by Soquimich, which announced plans to enter the cement business.

The blue-chip IPSA index ended 0.6 percent higher at 117.26 points. The all-share IGPA closed 0.27 percent higher on much lighter-than-average volume of 7.5 billion pesos, one of the lowest levels this year.
Brokers have reported listless trading all week.

"There are a lot of investors who have this idea that the bourse has already grown enough this year, and they don't think it's going to grow any more. That attitude and the drought are making the market very apathetic," one broker said, referring to concerns about the effect of drought on the electricity sector's second-quarter profits.
Electricity stocks were mixed, with some shares recovering from declines earlier this week. Endesa rebounded to end 1.9 percent up to 252.20 pesos, and Enersis closed 1.6 percent higher at 246 pesos.

Soquimich tumbled three percent to 2560 pesos after it announced plans for a $200 million push into the cement industry. The news was not well received by investors because it would pit the company -- the world's largest maker of iodine and a major producer of nitrates and lithium -- against some well-established rivals, brokers said.
"The cement market here is already too competitive. There is going to be a production glut," said one broker.
The market was awaiting economic growth figures to be announced Wednesday morning and first-quarter company results due out next week.
